issues.description: The solution's PersonResource constructor signature and implementation do not match the template/problem expectation: the template and the exercise expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService and assign it to the personService field, but the solution's constructor accepts a NoteService and sets personService to null. This breaks dependency injection and will cause runtime errors (null personService) and confuses readers comparing template, problem text and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the solution's PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService and assign it to the personService field, matching the template and problem specification. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }

issues.description: The solution implementation of PersonResource has a constructor that takes a NoteService parameter and assigns personService = null, while the template and the problem statement expect PersonResource to be injected with a PersonService. This mismatched identifier/type (NoteService vs PersonService) and the null assignment break the conceptual mapping between the REST resource and its backing service and will confuse students trying to follow the intended dependency injection and endpoint-to-service forwarding described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the PersonResource constructor in the solution to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field. Example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } This aligns the solution with the template and the problem statement.
